docs.title: Update infrastructure, not a framework.
docs.text: A lightweight Go update library with a release CLI and an optional sidecar for any language. Embed it, call Check, then Apply. Your application keeps its UI, lifecycle and restart behavior.

docs.title: Why WML Update
docs.text:
• Small public API

    New, Check, Apply, Close. No daemon, service locator, global state or required application architecture.

  • Verified artifacts

    Every download requires SHA-256. Optional Ed25519 manifests and checksums, HTTPS enforcement and host allowlists.

  • Transactional installs

    Staged directory/file swaps, crash recovery, backups and rollback data.

  • Windows-aware

    Deferred detached helper waits for the application to exit, then replaces and relaunches it.

  • Two sources

    GitHub Releases and self-hosted, signed static manifests.

  • Any language

    Non-Go applications use the same engine through NDJSON or a local HTTP API.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
go get github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate@v1.1.0

import wmlupdate "github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate"

u, err := wmlupdate.New(wmlupdate.Options{
    ConfigPath:     "updater.json",
    CurrentVersion: "1.4.2",
})
if err != nil { return err }
defer u.Close()

update, err := u.Check(ctx)
if err != nil || !update.Available { return err }

_, err = u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{})

Continue with the Go SDK guide, configuration, or take the sidecar path for Python, Node.js, C#, Java or shell.

docs.title: Release tooling
docs.text:
wml-update keygen --out-dir keys
wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out public/stable --key keys/signing-key.pem

Produces manifest.json, its Ed25519 signature, checksums.txt and a detached checksum signature. See self-hosting and GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. A small Go library that embeds in an existing application without taking over its architecture.
  2. One codebase covering Windows, macOS and Linux.
  3. A stable contract for non-Go languages through optional adapters.
  4. Authenticated metadata and verified artifacts.
  5. Safe, recoverable installation.
  6. Useful diagnostics, not silent failure.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• A framework or application runtime. The SDK exposes Check and Apply; the host owns UI, lifecycle and restart.
  • A required daemon or service. The CLI/HTTP adapters are optional.
  • Delta updates. A full artifact is downloaded; content-addressed caching avoids re-downloading the same bytes.
  • A system-wide scheduler. The host application decides when to check.
  • Arbitrary package-manager integration. The command strategy can invoke one, but rollback is owned by that installer.
  • Code signing. The updater preserves bytes; macOS notarization and Windows Authenticode signing remain part of your release pipeline.
  • A hosted update service. Any static web server is sufficient.

docs.title: Component map
docs.text:
github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate (package wmlupdate)
  └─ public SDK: New, Check, Apply, Options, Config, Event
       └─ internal/engine ──────── orchestration, checked snapshots, results
            ├─ internal/source ──┬─ github.go   Releases API + checksums
            │                    ├─ static.go   signed manifest + mirrors
            │                    └─ chain.go    ordered failover
            ├─ internal/httpx ──── hardened client, retry, resumable download
            ├─ internal/manifest  manifest model, validation, signature
            ├─ internal/checksum  SHA-256 and sha256sum parsing
            ├─ internal/install ─┬─ Prepare    staging / extract / preserve
            │                    └─ Apply      journal, backup, swap, rollback
            ├─ internal/archive   safe zip/tar extraction and creation
            ├─ internal/state     atomic JSON state and install journal
            ├─ internal/lock      per-app advisory lock
            └─ internal/sign      Ed25519 keys and detached signatures

cmd/wml-update
  └─ internal/cli ──────────────── commands, release tooling, sidecar adapter
       ├─ internal/engine ──────── same engine as the SDK
       └─ internal/api ─────────── optional loopback HTTP API, jobs, SSE

internal/publish ───────────────── release archive/manifest/checksum tooling

The SDK is the primary product. cmd/wml-update is optional: it packages releases (publish, keygen, sign, verify) and exposes the same engine to non-Go languages through NDJSON and HTTP. It does not participate in a Go application's runtime unless the application chooses the sidecar mode.

Supporting packages: internal/version (strict SemVer), internal/platform (normalization and asset heuristics), internal/event (event contract), internal/config (strict JSON loading, programmatic preparation, validation), internal/buildinfo (ldflags).

docs.title: Public SDK surface
docs.text:
type Options struct {
    ConfigPath, BaseDir, CurrentVersion string
    Config   *Config
    Platform *Platform
    Events   EventFunc
}

func New(Options) (*Updater, error)
func (*Updater) Check(context.Context) (*Update, error)
func (*Updater) Apply(context.Context, *Update, ApplyOptions) (*Result, error)
func (*Updater) Close()

Update is an opaque checked snapshot: public fields are informational, while the exact release and selected asset are retained privately. Apply validates and uses that snapshot, so a source change between Check and Apply cannot swap the artifact silently. Update values are not serializable.

docs.title: Update flow
docs.text:
Check / Apply
   │
   ├─ load strict config, resolve target platform
   ├─ determine current version (explicit > state > config)
   ├─ Check: fetch metadata, select asset, compare versions (read-only)
   ├─ Apply: acquire per-app lock
   ├─ recover interrupted transaction (if any)
   ├─ use the exact checked release snapshot (no metadata re-fetch)
   ├─ download to state/downloads with Range resume and retry
   ├─ verify size + SHA-256 (and authenticated hash source)
   ├─ install strategy:
   │    ├─ directory: extract → preserve → journal → swap → backup
   │    ├─ file:      stage → journal → backup → rename
   │    ├─ command:   run verified installer
   │    └─ external:  return artifact path
   └─ record state, optional relaunch, emit result

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text:
The source URL and configuration are trusted; everything fetched over the network is untrusted.

  1. Metadata authenticity
  2. Self-hosted manifests are signed with Ed25519 when a public key is configured. The signature covers the exact raw bytes, so whitespace and key ordering are not ambiguous.
  3. GitHub metadata is authenticated by TLS and the GitHub API. Hash strength is improved by requiring the API's asset digest or a checksums.txt asset. An optional signed checksums file provides an independent trust anchor.
  4. Artifact integrity
  5. Every download requires a SHA-256. Downloading is refused otherwise unless the dangerous allow_unverified_assets flag is set.
  6. The hash is taken from a signed manifest, a signed checksums file, or GitHub's API digest.
  7. Network boundaries
  8. HTTPS is required except loopback or explicit opt-in.
  9. Redirects are re-evaluated against scheme, host allowlist and count.
  10. Authorization headers are not forwarded to a different host by Go's redirect policy; self-hosted headers are only attached to same-host assets at the model layer.
  11. Filesystem safety
  12. Archive extraction rejects absolute paths, Windows volume paths, .. traversal, escaping symlinks, hardlinks, device/FIFO entries, duplicate symlink-parent writes, excessive entries and excessive expansion.
  13. Install targets are validated against filesystem root, the home directory, symlink targets and state-directory overlap.
  14. Staging and backups are siblings of the target, keeping renames on one filesystem.
  15. Local API
  16. Bearer token required, constant-time comparison.
  17. Loopback bind by default; remote binding requires an explicit flag.
  18. No CORS policy is added, so browser origins cannot call it cross-site without the token.

docs.title: Installation transaction
docs.text: State is kept in <state_dir>/state.json. Before any live rename, a pending journal records target, stage, backup, versions and phase.

docs.title: Directory / file replace
docs.text:
1. prepared: artifact verified, new tree staged; live target untouched.
  2. Rename target → backup (backed_up saved).
  3. Rename stage → target (committed saved).
  4. Append backup metadata, write installed version, clear journal.
  5. Prune backups beyond keep_backups.

On failure, the backup is restored. On the next mutating command, recovery inspects the journal:

  • prepared with backup present and target missing: restore backup.
  • backed_up with target present and stage gone: the swap completed; finalize.
  • Otherwise: restore the backup and remove partial staged data.
  • Command installers are not recoverable; the journal is cleared with a warning telling the operator to verify the application manually.

Backups are retained as siblings of the target so rollback requires only renames. rollback moves the current installation aside and restores the latest backup.

docs.title: Why a detached helper
docs.text:
On Windows, a running executable and loaded DLLs cannot be replaced, and the updater itself may live inside the application directory. With --defer:

  1. The parent updater downloads, verifies, extracts and writes a plan.
  2. It copies its own executable into the state directory.
  3. It starts the copied helper detached with --wait-pid values, then exits.
  4. The helper waits for the application to exit, acquires the lock, runs the same journaled apply path, optionally relaunches, and writes a result file.

This avoids depending on a helper inside the tree being replaced.

docs.title: State and concurrency
docs.text:
• One advisory lock per app_id serializes mutating operations across processes.
  • API jobs reject a second mutating job; the CLI additionally uses the file lock.
  • state.json writes are atomic (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync).
  • Source metadata uses ETag/Last-Modified caches stored under the state directory.
  • Downloads are named by expected SHA-256, so concurrent or repeated checks do not trust stale content.

docs.title: Result and event contract
docs.text:
--json writes one JSON object per line:

  • log, warning, progress: progress is download with bytes, total, percent.
  • result: exactly one terminal successful object.
  • error: terminal failure with a stable code.

The same shapes are returned by the HTTP job API. See integration.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Internal error / diagnostics failure 2 Usage or configuration error 3 Source, network, no release or no matching asset 4 Integrity / signature / checksum failure 5 Installation or rollback failure 6 Lock, state or I/O failure 130 Cancelled

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text:
• New source: implement source.Provider and normalize to release.Release.
  • New installer: add a strategy to config validation, Prepare and Apply, with a journal phase and rollback semantics.
  • New API: the engine is independent of Cobra and HTTP.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• ADR 0001: Go static binary
  • ADR 0002: subprocess NDJSON plus local HTTP (superseded as primary by 0005)
  • ADR 0003: transactional replace with backups
  • ADR 0004: supply-chain verification
  • ADR 0005: SDK-first public API
  • ADR 0006: ordered source chains

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
WML Update reads one JSON file. JSON is intentional: every language can generate it, it has no parser ambiguity, and unknown fields are rejected so typos fail loudly.

A JSON Schema is published at schema/config.schema.json. Editors that support $schema will autocomplete the file.

Go applications can either point the SDK at this file (Options.ConfigPath) or build the equivalent wmlupdate.Config in code. Programmatic durations use time.Duration; JSON uses duration strings such as "15m".

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
The configuration path is selected in this order:

  1. --config PATH / -c PATH
  2. WML_UPDATE_CONFIG environment variable
  3. ./updater.json
  4. ./.wml-update.json
  5. ./wml-update.json

Commands that do not operate on an installation (version, keygen, sign, verify, publish, the hidden __apply) do not require a config unless verify needs a default public key.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "app_id": "com.example.myapp",
  "channel": "stable",
  "current_version": "1.0.0",
  "source": {
    "type": "static",
    "manifest_url": "https://updates.example.com/stable/manifest.json"
  },
  "install": {
    "type": "directory",
    "path": "/opt/myapp"
  }
}

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text: Field Required Default Meaning $schema no — Editor schema hint; ignored by the updater schema_version no 1 Configuration schema version. Only 1 is accepted app_id yes — Stable identifier, [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127} channel no stable Logical channel / prerelease policy current_version no state Fallback current version source yes — Release discovery source asset_rules no auto-detect Platform asset selection rules install yes — Installation strategy state_dir no platform default State, cache, lock and download directory security no secure defaults Signatures, host allowlist, HTTP policy download no see below Size, timeout and retry limits

docs.title: Current version precedence
docs.text:
The version used for comparison comes from:

  1. --current-version on check, update, fetch and doctor
  2. installed_version recorded in updater state
  3. current_version in the configuration

If none is available, the command fails. Production applications should pass their compiled version on every invocation. State is preferred over the static config value so that repeated checks after an updater-driven installation do not keep comparing against a stale declared version; after a manual installation use mark or the flag. Config is the initial fallback.

Versions are strict SemVer 2.0.0. A leading v is accepted and removed. Build metadata is ignored for ordering.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
• Self-hosted: the manifest's channel must match the configured channel.
  • GitHub: stable ignores releases flagged prerelease and versions with a SemVer prerelease suffix. Any other channel includes prereleases. Setting source.include_prerelease to true also includes them.
  • --channel overrides the configured channel for one command.

docs.title: source
docs.text: Exactly one top-level source type is used. A source can itself be a chain of mirrors.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
{
  "type": "github",
  "owner": "acme",
  "repo": "myapp",
  "api_base": "https://api.github.com",
  "tag_prefix": "v",
  "token_env": "GITHUB_TOKEN",
  "include_prerelease": false
}
Field Required Notes owner, repo yes Repository coordinates api_base no GitHub Enterprise API base, default https://api.github.com tag_prefix no Strip this before SemVer parsing, e.g. v or myapp-v token_env no Environment variable with a token. If set but unset at runtime, the updater fails rather than silently hitting anonymous rate limits include_prerelease no Include prerelease releases regardless of channel

The provider reads up to 100 most recent releases, skips drafts, parses tags as SemVer, and selects the highest eligible version. Asset digests supplied by the GitHub API are used when no checksums.txt entry overrides them.

With a token configured, release assets are downloaded through the API asset endpoint, which supports private repositories. Without a token, public browser_download_urls are used.

docs.title: Static / self-hosted
docs.text:
{
  "type": "static",
  "manifest_url": "https://updates.example.com/stable/manifest.json",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer ${UPDATE_SERVER_TOKEN}"
  }
}
Field Required Notes manifest_url one of URL of manifest.json manifest_urls one of Ordered mirror URLs of the same manifest. The first usable mirror wins; relative assets are also resolved against the other bases for download failover headers no Extra request headers for the manifest, signature and same-host assets asset_mirrors no Asset URL templates tried when the primary asset host fails

When security.public_key or security.public_key_file is configured, the detached signature is fetched from <manifest_url>.sig and verified against the exact manifest bytes before parsing. A missing or invalid signature is fatal.

Headers are forwarded to assets only when the asset has the same host (including port) as the manifest. This prevents an authenticated manifest request from leaking credentials to a third-party CDN.

docs.title: Chain / automatic failover
docs.text:
{
  "type": "chain",
  "sources": [
    {
      "type": "github",
      "owner": "acme",
      "repo": "myapp",
      "tag_prefix": "v",
      "token_env": "GITHUB_TOKEN",
      "asset_mirrors": [
        "https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}/{asset}",
        "https://gitee.com/{owner}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}/{asset}"
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "static",
      "manifest_url": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/acme/myapp@main/updates/manifest.json"
    },
    {
      "type": "static",
      "manifest_url": "https://gitee.com/acme/myapp/raw/main/updates/manifest.json"
    },
    {
      "type": "static",
      "manifest_url": "https://updates.example.com/stable/manifest.json"
    }
  ]
}

chain.sources is ordered. The updater fetches metadata from each source until one returns a valid, authenticated release; later sources are fallbacks. A failure in one mirror does not abort the chain.

If metadata succeeds but the artifact download fails, the loader tries:

  1. the asset's own URL;
  2. asset_mirrors from the winning source;
  3. for relative static assets, the same path on the other manifest_urls;
  4. releases for the same version from the other chain sources.

Every fallback artifact must match the original checked SHA-256. A mirror can provide availability, never a different version or different bytes.

Mirror templates support:

Placeholder Value {url} Original absolute asset URL {owner}, {repo} GitHub coordinates (empty for static sources) {tag} Release tag, path-escaped {version} Normalized version, path-escaped {asset}, {name} Asset filename, path-escaped {os}, {arch} Target platform

Nested chains are rejected. Keep the first source authoritative and mirrors in sync; because metadata selection is first-success, a reachable but stale first mirror will be used rather than a newer fallback.

docs.title: Asset mirrors
docs.text:
asset_mirrors can be used without a chain, for example to keep GitHub Releases as the metadata source while downloading through a proxy:

{
  "type": "github",
  "owner": "acme",
  "repo": "myapp",
  "asset_mirrors": [
    "https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}/{asset}",
    "https://updates.example.com/{version}/{asset}"
  ]
}

Mirrors receive no source headers/token. Credentials are only sent to the asset URL's original host (and same-host fallbacks).

docs.title: asset_rules
docs.text:
GitHub assets have no platform metadata, and self-hosted manifests may omit it. Rules provide deterministic selection.

"asset_rules": [
  {
    "os": "darwin",
    "arch": "arm64",
    "match": "myapp-{version}-macos-arm64.zip",
    "format": "zip"
  },
  {
    "os": "windows",
    "arch": "amd64",
    "match": "myapp-{version}-windows-amd64.zip",
    "format": "zip"
  }
]

Rules are evaluated in order. A rule applies when its os/arch are empty or match the target platform. match is a Go path.Match glob applied to the asset name after replacing:

Placeholder Value {version} Normalized SemVer without v, e.g. 1.2.3 {tag} Raw source tag, e.g. v1.2.3 {os} Normalized OS: windows, darwin, linux {arch} Normalized architecture: amd64, arm64, ...

If a rule matches multiple assets, the command fails rather than guessing. format overrides the format inferred from the filename.

If no rule matches, selection proceeds as follows:

  1. A self-hosted manifest asset whose os and arch fields exactly match.
  2. A single architecture-neutral asset for the OS.
  3. A conservative filename heuristic (for example myapp-1.2.3-macos-arm64.zip).
  4. Otherwise, an error listing available assets.

Explicit rules are strongly recommended for production.

Supported formats: zip, tar.gz, tar, gz, raw, bin, exe, msi, pkg, dmg.

docs.title: directory
docs.text:
Replaces an entire application directory with the contents of a verified archive.

{
  "type": "directory",
  "path": "/opt/myapp",
  "strip_components": 1,
  "preserve": ["data/**", "config/**"],
  "keep_backups": 1,
  "relaunch_path": "/opt/myapp/bin/myapp",
  "relaunch_args": []
}
Field Default Meaning path — Target directory paths — Per-OS or per-OS-arch overrides strip_components 0 Leading archive path components to remove preserve [] Relative doublestar globs copied from the old install into the new tree keep_backups 1 Number of previous installations retained (0–10; 0 becomes 1 for replace strategies) relaunch_path — Executable started after a successful apply relaunch_args [] Arguments for relaunch; placeholders are expanded

The archive must be zip, tar or tar.gz. It is extracted into a sibling staging directory, preserved paths are copied in, and then the old directory is renamed to a backup and the staged directory is renamed into place. Both renames happen on the same filesystem.

The target directory is managed as a unit. Files present in the old install but absent from the new archive are removed unless a preserve pattern matches them. Symlinked targets are rejected. The filesystem root, the user home directory, and any path overlapping the state directory are rejected.

preserve patterns use doublestar syntax (*, **, ?, character classes). A matched directory preserves its whole subtree. Preserved content wins over content from the new archive at the same path.

Directory replacement preserves file modes from the archive and the target root's mode, but it does not copy ownership, ACLs, xattrs or resource forks from the previous tree. If those matter, create the install directory with the appropriate owner/ACL and use the command strategy with a platform package installer, or reapply metadata in a post-install step.

docs.title: macOS quarantine and ad-hoc signing
docs.text:
macOS may mark files as quarantined or report a modified bundle as damaged. Optional directory post-install handling is available:

{
  "type": "directory",
  "path": "/Applications/MyApp.app",
  "macos": {
    "remove_quarantine": true,
    "ad_hoc_sign": false,
    "allow_signer_change": false
  }
}
Field Default Meaning remove_quarantine false Run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the installed target. This bypasses Gatekeeper's first-launch evaluation ad_hoc_sign false Run codesign --force --deep --sign - on a .app target allow_signer_change false Permit replacing a signed .app with a bundle from a different Developer ID team

Both default off. remove_quarantine weakens a macOS security boundary and should only be enabled for updates whose source and SHA-256/Ed25519 trust you control. ad_hoc_sign destroys Developer ID signatures and notarization; use it only for unsigned app bundles, never for a notarized distribution. A quarantine-removal command failure is a warning; ad-hoc signing failure rolls back the directory swap. These actions only run when the updater itself is running on macOS.

When the installed target is a signed .app, the staged app must pass codesign --verify --deep --strict and have the same TeamIdentifier as the installed app. Set allow_signer_change only for an intentional Developer ID migration. Ad-hoc signing bypasses continuity because it deliberately replaces the signer.

docs.title: file
docs.text:
Replaces a single file, typically a standalone executable.

{
  "type": "file",
  "path": "C:\\Program Files\\MyApp\\myapp.exe",
  "file_mode": "0755",
  "keep_backups": 1
}

The new file is staged in the target directory, permissions are set from file_mode (or preserved from the existing file), and the old file is renamed to a backup before an atomic rename. The downloaded artifact is used as-is.

docs.title: command
docs.text:
Runs a platform installer after verification.

{
  "type": "command",
  "command": "msiexec.exe",
  "args": ["/i", "{artifact}", "/qn", "/norestart"],
  "timeout": "10m",
  "relaunch_path": "C:\\Program Files\\MyApp\\myapp.exe"
}

Placeholders:

Placeholder Value {artifact} Absolute path to the verified downloaded artifact {install_dir} / {target} Resolved install path (empty if none) {version} New version {previous_version} Current version {state_dir} State directory

command, arguments and environment values are expanded. The command is executed directly, not through a shell. Its combined stdout/stderr (up to 1 MiB) is reported. A non-zero exit or timeout fails the update. The installer owns rollback semantics; WML Update cannot roll back an arbitrary system installer.

docs.title: external
docs.text:
Downloads and verifies the artifact, then returns its path. The application installs it itself.

{"type": "external"}

After a successful custom install, call:

wml-update mark --version 1.2.0 --sha256 <artifact-sha256>

update with external returns status downloaded. fetch is the non-installing equivalent.

docs.title: Path selection
docs.text:
install.paths selects a path by target platform:

"paths": {
  "windows": "C:\\Program Files\\MyApp",
  "darwin": "/Applications/MyApp.app",
  "linux": "/opt/myapp",
  "linux-arm64": "/opt/myapp"
}

The exact os-arch key wins, then the os key, then path.

docs.title: Command placeholders and relaunch
docs.text: After a successful install, relaunch_path is started detached with relaunch_args. A relaunch failure is a warning: the update itself succeeded. The process is not waited for.

docs.title: security
docs.text:
{
  "public_key": "",
  "public_key_file": "keys/signing-key.pub.pem",
  "checksums_asset": "checksums.txt",
  "checksums_signature_asset": "checksums.txt.sig",
  "allowed_hosts": ["api.github.com", "github.com", "objects.githubusercontent.com", "release-assets.githubusercontent.com"],
  "allow_insecure_http": false,
  "allow_unverified_assets": false
}
Field Default Meaning public_key — Inline PEM or base64 raw Ed25519 public key public_key_file — Public key file, relative to this config checksums_asset checksums.txt GitHub release checksum asset name checksums_signature_asset <checksums_asset>.sig GitHub checksum signature asset allowed_hosts [] Optional allowlist for every request and redirect allow_insecure_http false Permit plain HTTP to non-loopback hosts allow_unverified_assets false Permit downloads with no known SHA-256 (dangerous)

Set only one of public_key and public_key_file.

When a public key is configured:

  • Self-hosted sources require a valid <manifest_url>.sig.
  • GitHub sources require both checksum and signature assets. The signature is verified over the exact checksum bytes before hashes are trusted.

allowed_hosts accepts exact hosts, hosts with ports, and wildcard subdomains such as *.example.com. It also applies to redirects. For GitHub downloads you must include the asset redirect hosts you use.

allow_unverified_assets is a last-resort escape hatch. It prints a warning and records the computed SHA-256, but it cannot authenticate what was downloaded.

docs.title: download
docs.text:
{
  "max_bytes": 2147483648,
  "timeout": "30m",
  "retries": 3,
  "proxy": "http://127.0.0.1:7890"
}
Field Default Meaning max_bytes 2 GiB Maximum artifact size and extraction-expansion budget timeout 30m Overall HTTP client timeout retries 3 Retries for transient source/download failures (0–10) proxy env Explicit HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 or SOCKS5H proxy. Overrides HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY. Supports ${ENV_VAR}

Retries honor Retry-After for 429/503 responses. Downloads resume from a .part file using HTTP Range requests. A final file only appears after size and SHA-256 verification.

A configured proxy applies to metadata, signatures, artifacts and redirects. Proxy credentials are not logged. An explicit proxy is trusted configuration; the proxy can observe destination hosts and URLs.

docs.title: Environment expansion and paths
docs.text:
${NAME} and $NAME are expanded in selected configuration fields. Referencing an unset variable is an error, not a silent empty string. Expansion applies to:

  • current_version
  • source.manifest_url
  • source.headers values
  • security.public_key_file
  • state_dir
  • install.path, install.paths, install.workdir, install.relaunch_path
  • install.env values

A leading ~ and ~/ in paths are expanded to the current home directory. Relative paths resolve against the configuration file's directory, not the process working directory.

Command-line --os and --arch override the target platform for selection and path resolution. This is useful for testing cross-platform packages.

docs.title: Default state directories
docs.text:
OS Default Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\wml-update\<app_id> macOS ~/Library/Application Support/wml-update/<app_id> Linux/BSD $XDG_STATE_HOME/wml-update/<app_id> or ~/.local/state/wml-update/<app_id>

The state directory contains state.json, the update lock, source metadata cache, partial/final downloads, helper plans and backups (backups themselves are siblings of the install target). It is created with owner-only permissions.

docs.title: Frequent releases
docs.text:
WML Update is designed for channels that publish often, including several builds per day. The library itself does not schedule checks or impose a release cadence; the host application decides when to check, and the update feed is just static metadata with hashes and optional signatures.

This model follows the approach used by fast-moving desktop apps: a dedicated feed, immutable version numbers, background staging, and a deliberate restart.

docs.title: This project's own nightly channel
docs.text:
The repository includes .github/workflows/nightly.yml. On its daily schedule (or a manual workflow_dispatch) it:

  1. runs the test suite;
  2. derives the next minor from the newest reachable stable tag, e.g. stable v1.1.0 becomes base v1.2.0;
  3. tags the current main as vX.Y.0-nightly.YYYYMMDD.<run-number>.<attempt>;
  4. builds and publishes a GitHub prerelease with the normal archives, packages, checksums and (when configured) checksums.txt.sig.

Nightly tags are valid SemVer prereleases. Stable clients ignore them; a nightly client opts in explicitly. The docs workflow does not publish a docs version for nightly tags; latest remains the newest stable release.

The workflow does not create a new stable release or move latest. Stable releases stay deliberate, annotated tags.

docs.title: Publish a dedicated feed, not a GitHub API call per check
docs.text:
Use a static manifest (or a small dynamic endpoint serving the same shape) for the hot path:

https://updates.example.com/nightly/manifest.json
https://updates.example.com/nightly/myapp-1.8.1341-linux-amd64.tar.gz

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "app_id": "com.example.myapp",
  "channel": "nightly",
  "version": "1.8.1341",
  "published_at": "2026-10-28T08:00:00Z",
  "notes": "Nightly build",
  "assets": [
    {
      "name": "myapp-1.8.1341-linux-amd64.tar.gz",
      "os": "linux",
      "arch": "amd64",
      "url": "myapp-1.8.1341-linux-amd64.tar.gz",
      "sha256": "<64 hex characters>",
      "size": 12345678,
      "format": "tar.gz"
    }
  ]
}

A manifest fetch is small, cacheable with ETag/Last-Modified, and sidesteps GitHub API rate limits. Mirror it through a source.type: chain for availability.

docs.title: Version every build uniquely
docs.text:
• Use a monotonic SemVer patch/build counter, e.g. 1.8.1341 → 1.8.1342.
  • Do not rely on build metadata (1.8.1341+sha) to distinguish versions; SemVer ignores build metadata in ordering.
  • Pre-releases use 1.9.0-beta.3, not an arbitrary suffix.
  • The manifest version must match the asset content. Never reuse a version with different bytes.

The updater refuses downgrades by default and uses the exact SHA-256 from the checked manifest.

docs.title: Keep channels separate
docs.text:
Publish separate manifests for stable, beta and nightly:

https://updates.example.com/stable/manifest.json
https://updates.example.com/beta/manifest.json
https://updates.example.com/nightly/manifest.json

The manifest channel must match the client's configured channel. "Stable" policy (weekly promotion, holdbacks, urgent releases) belongs in your release service; WML Update only consumes the selected feed.

docs.title: Check on the host's schedule
docs.text:
The SDK has no background loop by design. A host can check at startup and then every N minutes:

ticker := time.NewTicker(6 * time.Hour)
defer ticker.Stop()

for {
    select {
    case <-ctx.Done():
        return
    case <-ticker.C:
        update, err := u.Check(ctx)
        if err != nil || !update.Available {
            continue
        }
        // Stage now. The helper installs when the application exits and retries
        // the relaunch, so a long-running app does not need to restart now.
        if _, err := u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{
            Defer:    true,
            WaitPIDs: []int{os.Getpid()},
        }); err != nil {
            log.Printf("update staging failed [%s]: %v", wmlupdate.Code(err), err)
        }
        return
    }
}

Call the deferred apply once per checked version. If the app stays alive, the helper waits; a later check that stages another version would create another helper, so the host should either exit or avoid scheduling a second one until the first is consumed.

For applications that own their installation, use install.type=external and call Apply; the result contains the verified artifact path.

docs.title: Stage safely
docs.text:
• Download and verify before touching the live tree.
  • Keep the previous backup for rollback.
  • On Windows, use ApplyOptions{Defer: true, WaitPIDs: ...}; the detached helper waits for the app, retries transient file-sharing failures, and can relaunch.
  • On macOS, verify signer continuity for signed .app bundles; optionally remove quarantine or ad-hoc sign only for unsigned distributions.
  • Do not auto-remove quarantine on a channel you do not control.

docs.title: Make availability independent of one host
docs.text:
{
  "source": {
    "type": "chain",
    "sources": [
      {
        "type": "static",
        "manifest_urls": [
          "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/acme/myapp@main/updates/nightly/manifest.json",
          "https://gitee.com/acme/myapp/raw/main/updates/nightly/manifest.json",
          "https://updates.example.com/nightly/manifest.json"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Downloads try the asset URL, asset_mirrors, other manifest bases, and same-version chain sources. A fallback must match the checked SHA-256.

docs.title: Publication order
docs.text:
1. Upload versioned assets.
  2. Upload manifest.json.sig.
  3. Upload manifest.json last.

Keep old manifests and assets available for clients that are mid-update and for operational rollback. Clients with long update intervals should pin their channel manifest separately.

docs.title: Avoid making every check download
docs.text:
The SDK separates discovery from installation:

  • Check fetches metadata only.
  • Apply downloads and stages, or installs immediately.
  • A checksum-addressed download cache makes repeated attempts idempotent.

Do not treat an update check as a request to restart. Let the host decide when the user is ready; the deferred helper handles the eventual exit.

docs.title: What this borrows from fast updaters
docs.text:
The design adopts the operational lessons of high-frequency desktop updaters:

  • a dedicated feed separate from the code host;
  • immutable, unique versions;
  • mirror and proxy support with hash-bound fallback;
  • background staging and a restart deferred to the host;
  • Windows file-sharing and antivirus retries;
  • macOS signer continuity and relaunch retries;
  • old-version retention for rollback.

It deliberately leaves scheduling, UI prompts and restart policy to the embedding application.

docs.title: GitHub Releases
docs.text: GitHub releases are the fastest way to ship updates. The updater works with public repositories out of the box and with private repositories when a token is configured.

docs.title: Release naming
docs.text:
Use a SemVer tag, optionally with a prefix:

v1.5.0
myapp-v1.5.0

Set source.tag_prefix when there is a prefix. A leading v is accepted even without a prefix setting.

Attach one asset per platform/architecture. Either name them so the built-in heuristic can find them:

myapp-1.5.0-macos-arm64.zip
myapp-1.5.0-macos-amd64.zip
myapp-1.5.0-windows-amd64.zip
myapp-1.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
myapp-1.5.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz

or, preferably, declare explicit rules:

"asset_rules": [
  {"os": "darwin",  "arch": "arm64", "match": "myapp-{version}-macos-arm64.zip", "format": "zip"},
  {"os": "darwin",  "arch": "amd64", "match": "myapp-{version}-macos-amd64.zip", "format": "zip"},
  {"os": "windows", "arch": "amd64", "match": "myapp-{version}-windows-amd64.zip", "format": "zip"},
  {"os": "linux",   "arch": "amd64", "match": "myapp-{version}-linux-amd64.tar.gz", "format": "tar.gz"}
]

If multiple assets match for the target platform, the updater fails rather than guessing.

docs.title: Hashes
docs.text:
A GitHub release should include a checksums.txt asset in GNU format:

<sha256>  myapp-1.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
<sha256>  myapp-1.5.0-macos-arm64.zip
<sha256>  myapp-1.5.0-windows-amd64.zip

The publish command writes this file alongside a manifest:

wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out dist --key signing-key.pem

Upload dist/checksums.txt to the release. The updater also consumes GitHub API digest fields when present. If neither a checksum entry nor a digest exists for the selected asset, the update is refused.

docs.title: Signed checksums (recommended)
docs.text:
wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out dist --key signing-key.pem

Upload both:

  • checksums.txt
  • checksums.txt.sig

Then configure:

"security": {
  "public_key_file": "keys/signing-key.pub.pem",
  "checksums_asset": "checksums.txt",
  "checksums_signature_asset": "checksums.txt.sig"
}

When a public key is configured, a missing or invalid signature is fatal. The signature covers the exact checksum file bytes. Individual artifact signatures are unnecessary because the signed checksum file authenticates every hash.

Do not attach manifest.json to a GitHub release unless you want it as a separate convenience; GitHub sources read release assets directly and ignore self-hosted manifests.

docs.title: Channels and prereleases
docs.text:
• Configured channel stable: skip releases with GitHub's prerelease flag and tags containing SemVer prereleases (v1.5.0-rc.1).
  • Any other channel, or source.include_prerelease: true: include both stable and prerelease builds, selecting the highest SemVer.
  • Draft releases are always skipped.

Tags that are not valid SemVer are skipped, not coerced.

docs.title: Private repositories
docs.text:
Create a fine-grained or classic token with read access to releases for that repository. Do not put the token in the JSON file:

"source": {
  "type": "github",
  "owner": "acme",
  "repo": "private-app",
  "token_env": "GITHUB_TOKEN"
}

At runtime, GITHUB_TOKEN must be present. If it is configured but missing, the updater fails clearly instead of silently falling back to anonymous rate limits.

Asset downloads go through the GitHub API asset endpoint with Accept: application/octet-stream, which supports private release assets. Go's HTTP client strips the Authorization header when GitHub redirects to signed storage, so the token is not leaked to the CDN.

For public repositories, a token is optional but strongly recommended to avoid the 60 requests/hour anonymous limit. The updater surfaces rate-limit errors with guidance.

docs.title: Mirrors and automatic failover
docs.text:
GitHub API/asset access can be blocked independently. Use an ordered chain with static mirrors for metadata and asset templates for downloads:

{
  "source": {
    "type": "chain",
    "sources": [
      {
        "type": "github",
        "owner": "acme",
        "repo": "myapp",
        "tag_prefix": "v",
        "token_env": "GITHUB_TOKEN",
        "asset_mirrors": [
          "https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}/{asset}",
          "https://gitee.com/{owner}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}/{asset}"
        ]
      },
      {
        "type": "static",
        "manifest_urls": [
          "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/acme/myapp@main/updates/manifest.json",
          "https://gitee.com/acme/myapp/raw/main/updates/manifest.json",
          "https://updates.example.com/stable/manifest.json"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Metadata is tried in order. After a successful check, the artifact tries its original URL, configured asset mirrors, and same-version assets from the other chain sources. Every fallback must match the checked SHA-256; mirrors cannot change the version or bytes. Mirrors do not receive GitHub tokens or source headers.

See configuration for placeholders and first-success semantics.

docs.title: Network allowlist
docs.text:
If you set security.allowed_hosts, include every host involved in metadata and redirects. A typical set is:

"allowed_hosts": [
  "api.github.com",
  "github.com",
  "objects.githubusercontent.com",
  "release-assets.githubusercontent.com"
]

The exact asset redirect host can vary. If you do not need an allowlist, leave it empty. It is still protected by HTTPS and signature/hash verification.

For GitHub Enterprise, set source.api_base to your instance's API base and include that host in allowed_hosts.

docs.title: CI example
docs.text:
name: release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - name: Build artifacts
        run: ./scripts/build-release.sh   # your cross-build
      - name: Generate signed checksums
        env:
          WML_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.WML_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          umask 077
          printf '%s' "$WML_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/key.pem"
          wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out dist --key "$RUNNER_TEMP/key.pem"
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/key.pem"
      - name: Create release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" dist/* \
            --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" \
            --notes-file release-notes.md

publish signs checksums.txt even if you only use the GitHub source, so the same build output works for self-hosting later.

docs.title: Updating WML Update itself
docs.text:
The project's release workflow builds one archive per platform, each containing wml-update, LICENSE and README.md. A self-update config can install the archive into a dedicated tool directory:

{
  "app_id": "dev.wml.update",
  "channel": "stable",
  "source": {
    "type": "github",
    "owner": "yxxbc",
    "repo": "wmlUpdate",
    "tag_prefix": "v"
  },
  "asset_rules": [
    {"os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "match": "wml-update_{version}_linux_amd64.tar.gz", "format": "tar.gz"},
    {"os": "darwin", "arch": "arm64", "match": "wml-update_{version}_darwin_arm64.tar.gz", "format": "tar.gz"},
    {"os": "windows", "arch": "amd64", "match": "wml-update_{version}_windows_amd64.zip", "format": "zip"}
  ],
  "install": {
    "type": "directory",
    "paths": {
      "linux": "/opt/wml-update",
      "darwin": "/usr/local/opt/wml-update",
      "windows": "C:\\Tools\\wml-update"
    },
    "strip_components": 0
  }
}

The target must be a directory dedicated to the updater; directory installs replace the whole tree. On Windows, run with --defer --wait-pid <pid> because the updater binary itself may be running.

For a single raw binary, publish a raw artifact (not a zip/tar archive) and use:

"install": {"type": "file", "path": "/home/me/.local/bin/wml-update"}

The file strategy installs the downloaded artifact as-is; it does not unpack archives.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The provider reads the 100 most recent releases. If the newest eligible release is older than that in a burst of non-SemVer tags, it may not be seen.
  • GitHub's API is paginated; 100 is the maximum page size used.
  • GitHub releases have no custom channels beyond prerelease/stable. Use tags, separate repositories, or self-hosted manifests for arbitrary channels.

docs.title: Integration guide
docs.text:
There are three supported integration surfaces. All use the same engine and the same result/error semantics.

  1. Go library — preferred for Go applications. Two calls, no daemon, no process boundary.
  2. Subprocess + NDJSON — universal fallback for other languages, process isolation, or embedding in non-Go build systems.
  3. Loopback HTTP API — for desktop apps that want a long-lived updater process, job polling, cancellation and SSE.

docs.title: Go library
docs.text:
Import the module and keep the integration to New, Check and Apply:

import wmlupdate "github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate"

u, err := wmlupdate.New(wmlupdate.Options{
    ConfigPath:     "updater.json",
    CurrentVersion: appVersion,
})
if err != nil { return err }
defer u.Close()

update, err := u.Check(ctx)
if err != nil { return err }
if !update.Available { return nil }

result, err := u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{})

Options.Config can replace ConfigPath for a dependency-only setup. Events are an optional callback. The library never exits or restarts the host. See the Go SDK guide for the complete API, Windows deferred apply, programmatic configuration and error codes.

docs.title: Subprocess + NDJSON
docs.text:
Run the binary directly. Do not invoke it through a shell: paths, arguments and exit codes are safer when passed as an argv array.

wml-update --config /path/updater.json --json update --current-version 1.4.2

When --json is set:

  • stdout contains only JSON objects, one per line.
  • stderr contains human diagnostics, if any.
  • Never parse prose from stdout.
  • Read stdout line by line as the process runs; do not wait for exit before displaying progress.
  • Treat the terminal result or error event as authoritative, and also check the process exit code.

docs.title: Event shapes
docs.text:
Progress:

{"type":"progress","time":"2026-10-28T12:00:00Z","phase":"download","bytes":1048576,"total":4194304,"percent":25}

Log and warning:

{"type":"log","time":"2026-10-28T12:00:00Z","phase":"source","message":"querying static source"}
{"type":"warning","time":"2026-10-28T12:00:00Z","message":"artifact has no SHA-256; security.allow_unverified_assets is enabled"}

Success:

{
  "type": "result",
  "time": "2026-10-28T12:00:01Z",
  "data": {
    "status": "updated",
    "current_version": "1.5.0",
    "previous_version": "1.4.2",
    "latest_version": "1.5.0",
    "channel": "stable",
    "source": "static",
    "tag": "1.5.0",
    "published_at": "2026-10-27T09:00:00Z",
    "notes": "Release notes",
    "asset": {
      "name": "myapp-1.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz",
      "os": "linux",
      "arch": "amd64",
      "format": "tar.gz",
      "sha256": "0123...",
      "size": 4194304
    },
    "artifact_path": "/home/user/.local/state/wml-update/com.example.myapp/downloads/0123...__myapp-1.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
  }
}

Failure:

{"type":"error","time":"2026-10-28T12:00:01Z","error":{"code":"integrity","message":"checksum mismatch: got ..., want ..."}}

docs.title: Status values
docs.text:
Status Command Meaning update_available check, update --dry-run A newer (or forced) release is available up_to_date check, update, fetch Current version is not older than the release updated update Installation completed downloaded update with install.type=external, fetch Verified artifact is available at artifact_path apply_scheduled update --defer Staged; detached helper will apply it rolled_back rollback Previous backup restored marked mark External installation recorded

check exits 0 even when an update is available. Branch on result.data.status.

docs.title: Error codes and exit codes
docs.text: Code Exit Meaning config 2 Invalid config, version or flags source / network 3 Source unavailable, malformed response, HTTP failure no_release / no_asset 3 Nothing eligible / no asset for this platform integrity 4 Signature, checksum or size failure install / rollback 5 Filesystem/install failure locked / state / io 6 Concurrent update, state or I/O failure cancelled 130 Context/signal cancellation internal 1 Unexpected error

docs.title: Choosing a command
docs.text:
• check is cheap and read-only. Use it on startup or a timer.
  • update is the normal path: check + download + verify + install.
  • fetch --output PATH verifies an artifact and copies it to a path so your code can install it. Follow with mark --version ... --sha256 ... only after your installer succeeds.
  • update --defer is required when the target is running on Windows.

docs.title: Deferred apply (Windows and self-replacement)
docs.text:
app process ──spawn──> wml-update update --defer --wait-pid <appPID> --json
    │                         │
    │                         ├─ download, verify, extract, write plan
    │                         ├─ copy updater to state dir/helper/<plan>/
    │                         ├─ start helper detached
    │                         └─ emit result apply_scheduled; exit 0
    │
    └─ exits (after receiving apply_scheduled)

helper ── waits for <appPID> ── acquires lock ── journaled apply ── relaunch

Recommended sequence:

  1. Spawn the updater with update --defer --wait-pid <yourPID> --json.
  2. Read until the result event.
  3. If status == "apply_scheduled", exit the application promptly.
  4. Configure install.relaunch_path so the helper restarts the new version.

The parent updater must be allowed to finish emitting apply_scheduled before the application exits. The helper is copied outside the managed directory, so it can replace files even when the updater binary itself lives inside the target.

A helper result file is written at:

<state_dir>/plans/<plan_id>.json.result

with {"ok":true} or an error. On failure the plan is retained for diagnosis; the next update recovers any pending journal.

docs.title: Language examples
docs.text:
• Python
  • Node.js
  • Go sidecar
  • C#
  • Shell

All examples follow the same rules: argv array, line-delimited JSON, wait for a terminal event, check the exit code.

docs.title: Loopback HTTP API
docs.text:
Start the server:

wml-update --config updater.json serve --json

Example ready line (a token is generated when none is supplied):

{"type":"ready","url":"http://127.0.0.1:52143","address":"127.0.0.1:52143","pid":4242,"token_source":"generated","token":"..."}

If a token is supplied with --token, --token-env or --token-file, it is not echoed; the caller already knows it. WML_UPDATE_TOKEN is read automatically if no flag is set.

The server binds loopback by default. --allow-remote permits another address; terminate TLS and additional authentication at a reverse proxy.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every endpoint except /v1/health requires one of:

Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-WML-Token: <token>

Tokens must be at least 16 characters. Comparison is constant-time. There is no CORS opt-in.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose GET /v1/health Liveness; no auth GET /v1/info App ID, channel, platform, source type GET /v1/status Persisted state POST /v1/check Synchronous check POST /v1/update Start asynchronous update job POST /v1/fetch Start asynchronous verified-download job POST /v1/rollback Start asynchronous rollback job POST /v1/mark Record an externally installed version GET /v1/jobs List jobs GET /v1/jobs/{id} Job snapshot with events POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel Cancel a running job GET /v1/jobs/{id}/events SSE event stream

Only one mutating job (update, fetch, rollback) can run at a time. A second returns HTTP 409 with code job_conflict.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
POST /v1/check
Authorization: Bearer ...
Content-Type: application/json

{"current_version":"1.4.2"}

Returns the same result object used by the CLI (status, versions, notes, asset). HTTP status reflects whether the check itself succeeded; up_to_date is a 200, not an error.

docs.title: Update job
docs.text:
POST /v1/update
Authorization: Bearer ...

{
  "current_version": "1.4.2",
  "force": false,
  "defer": false,
  "wait_pids": []
}

Returns HTTP 202:

{
  "id": "9d3f...",
  "kind": "update",
  "status": "running",
  "created_at": "2026-10-28T12:00:00Z"
}

Poll GET /v1/jobs/{id}:

{
  "id": "9d3f...",
  "kind": "update",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "result": {"status":"updated","previous_version":"1.4.2","current_version":"1.5.0"},
  "events": [
    {"type":"progress","phase":"download","bytes":100,"total":100,"percent":100},
    {"type":"log","phase":"install","message":"artifact staged"}
  ]
}

status is running, succeeded, failed or cancelled. Errors use error.code and error.message with the same stable codes as the CLI.

docs.title: SSE events
docs.text:
GET /v1/jobs/{id}/events
Authorization: Bearer ...
Accept: text/event-stream

Each event is an SSE data: frame containing the same JSON event object. The job emits a terminal result or error event, then the stream closes after all buffered events are delivered. The server polls internally every 250 ms. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID to resume by index.

docs.title: Minimal Python HTTP client
docs.text:
import json, urllib.request

def call(base, token, path, payload=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        base + path,
        data=json.dumps(payload or {}).encode(),
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + token, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST" if payload is not None else "GET",
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
        return json.load(r)

docs.title: Concurrency and lifetime
docs.text:
• The CLI is safe to call concurrently; the per-app file lock serializes writes.
  • The HTTP API keeps jobs in memory and loses them on restart. Call /v1/status for durable state.
  • Cancel is cooperative: it cancels the context, which stops downloads and source requests. A filesystem apply already in progress is short and may finish; rollback remains available.

docs.title: Self-hosted manifest format
docs.text:
A self-hosted update channel is a static directory containing:

manifest.json
manifest.json.sig        # required when a public key is configured
checksums.txt            # generated for GitHub releases; optional for static hosts
checksums.txt.sig        # optional signed checksums
myapp-1.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
myapp-1.2.0-windows-amd64.zip
...

The updater fetches manifest.json, verifies the detached signature when a public key is configured, validates the manifest, selects the asset for the running platform, and uses the manifest's SHA-256 to verify the download.

JSON Schema: schema/manifest.schema.json.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "app_id": "com.example.myapp",
  "channel": "stable",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "published_at": "2026-10-28T12:00:00Z",
  "notes": "Fixes and performance improvements.",
  "mandatory": false,
  "assets": [
    {
      "name": "myapp-1.2.0-macos-arm64.zip",
      "os": "darwin",
      "arch": "arm64",
      "url": "myapp-1.2.0-macos-arm64.zip",
      "sha256": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "size": 18432000,
      "format": "zip"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Required Notes schema_version yes Must be 1 app_id yes Must equal the updater configuration's app_id channel yes Must equal the configured channel (case-insensitive) version yes Strict SemVer 2.0.0, with optional leading v published_at no RFC 3339 timestamp notes no Release notes, at most 1 MiB mandatory no Passed through to the client UI; the CLI does not force installation assets yes 1–256 entries

docs.title: Asset fields
docs.text:
Field Required Notes url yes Absolute, or relative to manifest.json sha256 yes 64 hexadecimal characters name no Defaults to the URL basename; used by asset_rules and checksums os no Go-style OS (windows, darwin, linux) or common aliases arch no Go-style architecture (amd64, arm64, ...) or common aliases size no Byte size; when present, enforced before and after download format no zip, tar.gz, tar, gz, raw, exe, msi, pkg, dmg

Relative URLs resolve against the manifest URL. Asset metadata is used when no asset_rules match. asset_rules always take priority.

Unknown fields are rejected.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text:
Signatures are detached Ed25519 signatures over the exact bytes of the file. The signature file is standard-base64 text (raw 64-byte signatures are also accepted when verifying).

wml-update keygen --out-dir keys
wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out public/stable --key keys/signing-key.pem
wml-update verify --manifest --public-key-file keys/signing-key.pub.pem public/stable/manifest.json

Outputs:

  • manifest.json
  • manifest.json.sig
  • checksums.txt (GNU sha256sum format, sorted by asset name)
  • checksums.txt.sig when signing is enabled

The public key goes into the client configuration:

"security": { "public_key_file": "keys/signing-key.pub.pem" }

or as an inline base64 raw key:

"security": { "public_key": "base64-encoded-32-byte-key" }

The client fetches <manifest_url>.sig. A manifest with a missing, malformed or invalid signature is rejected before any JSON parsing or asset URL resolution. Treat the private key as a release credential: store it in a secret manager or CI protected secret, never in the web root.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
publish reads a spec relative to the spec file and writes into --out:

wml-update publish \
  --spec publish.json \
  --out public/stable \
  --key ../keys/signing-key.pem \
  --base-url https://updates.example.com/stable

Spec:

{
  "app_id": "com.example.myapp",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "channel": "stable",
  "notes_file": "CHANGELOG.md",
  "assets": [
    {
      "dir": "dist/MyApp",
      "url": "myapp-1.2.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz",
      "os": "linux",
      "arch": "amd64",
      "format": "tar.gz"
    },
    {
      "path": "dist/MyApp.exe",
      "url": "myapp-1.2.0-windows-amd64.exe",
      "os": "windows",
      "arch": "amd64",
      "format": "raw"
    }
  ]
}

Each asset sets exactly one of dir (archive it) or path (copy the prebuilt file). url is the relative output path and the default manifest asset name. name overrides the manifest name. base_url (or --base-url) prepends a public URL to every asset URL; without it, URLs remain relative to the manifest.

If a signing key is supplied, checksums.txt.sig is also written. GitHub releases can upload checksums.txt and checksums.txt.sig directly.

docs.title: Deployment notes
docs.text:
• Upload artifacts first, then manifest.json, then manifest.json.sig. Never expose a manifest that references bytes not yet present.
  • Use a short cache lifetime for manifest.json and immutable, long-lived cache headers for versioned assets.
  • The updater uses ETag / Last-Modified conditional requests for manifests.
  • Keep previous manifests and artifacts for rollback of the update service.
  • Use TLS. Plain HTTP is only accepted for loopback or with an explicit client opt-in.
  • If assets live on a different host and require credentials, do not put those credentials in source.headers: headers are only forwarded to the manifest's own host. Use a public CDN or a host that does not require the secret.

docs.title: Release signing
docs.text: The project's own release checksums are signed with an Ed25519 key. This key is for WML Update releases, not for applications embedding the library. Every application should generate its own key with wml-update keygen.

docs.title: Public key
docs.text:
• Public key
  • Raw form: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate/main/signing/release-signing-key.pub.pem
  • DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo SHA-256 fingerprint:
082733d41a311c633e30d4a5603822db65a48ef12be498e38a0a22edeb6a9b55

Each release includes checksums.txt and checksums.txt.sig, a detached signature over the exact checksum file bytes.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
With an existing binary:

wml-update verify \
  --public-key-file signing/release-signing-key.pub.pem \
  checksums.txt

Independently with OpenSSL:

openssl base64 -d -A -in checksums.txt.sig -out /tmp/checksums.sig
openssl pkeyutl -verify -pubin \
  -inkey signing/release-signing-key.pub.pem \
  -rawin -in checksums.txt -sigfile /tmp/checksums.sig

Fetch the public key from the tagged release or a trusted commit, never from an unverified mirror.

docs.title: Private key custody
docs.text:
The private key must never enter git, an artifact, a shell transcript, an issue or an unencrypted backup.

Copy Location CI GitHub Actions secret WML_SIGNING_KEY; enable with variable WML_SIGNING_ENABLED=true Local macOS backup ~/.config/wml-update/release-signing-key.pem (mode 0600) macOS Keychain service wml-update-release-signing-key, account yxxbc

GitHub secrets are write-only. Store the key in a password manager or encrypted offline backup as well. A lost private key cannot be recovered from GitHub.

docs.title: Retrieve from macOS Keychain
docs.text:
security returns generic-password data as hex when it contains line breaks:

security find-generic-password \
  -s wml-update-release-signing-key -w | xxd -r -p \
  > release-signing-key.pem
chmod 600 release-signing-key.pem

The login Keychain item is local to the Mac unless iCloud Keychain is enabled and the item is added through Apple Passwords/Keychain Access. For cross-device recovery, also store the PEM in Apple Passwords (as a secure note/password) or a password manager.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
1. Generate a new pair with wml-update keygen.
  2. Publish the new public key and fingerprint before switching the CI secret.
  3. Keep the old public key available for verifying historical releases.
  4. Update WML_SIGNING_KEY and WML_SIGNING_ENABLED.
  5. Never overwrite the private key without an offline backup.

docs.title: Go SDK
docs.text:
API reference on pkg.go.dev

The Go package is the primary integration surface. It is a library, not a framework: no daemon, no required directory layout, no lifecycle hooks and no global state. Your application owns startup, UI, process exit and restart.

import wmlupdate "github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate"

docs.title: Design contract
docs.text:
The public API is intentionally two operations:

update, err := u.Check(ctx)     // discover and select a release
result, err := u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{})

Check performs no writes to the application tree. Apply downloads, verifies and installs a previously checked release. Progress is optional through a callback; the terminal outcome is the return value.

The library also uses a small state directory for locks, downloads, backups and recovery. That is internal bookkeeping, not a requirement on your application structure.

docs.title: Minimal integration
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "os"

    wmlupdate "github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate"
)

func checkForUpdates(ctx context.Context) error {
    u, err := wmlupdate.New(wmlupdate.Options{
        ConfigPath:     "updater.json",
        CurrentVersion: appVersion,
        Events: func(e wmlupdate.Event) {
            if e.Type == wmlupdate.EventProgress && e.Phase == "download" {
                fmt.Printf("\r%d%%", int(e.Percent))
            }
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer u.Close()

    update, err := u.Check(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if !update.Available {
        return nil
    }

    result, err := u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{})
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    fmt.Printf("\ninstalled %s (was %s)\n", result.Version, result.PreviousVersion)
    return nil
}

That is the whole integration. Your UI decides whether to prompt, when to check, and when to restart.

docs.title: From updater.json
docs.text:
Options.ConfigPath loads the same configuration format used by the CLI, including environment expansion, signature keys and all install strategies.

u, err := wmlupdate.New(wmlupdate.Options{
    ConfigPath:     "/path/to/updater.json",
    CurrentVersion: "1.4.2",
})

docs.title: Programmatic
docs.text:
For a dependency-only setup, avoid shipping a separate config file:

u, err := wmlupdate.New(wmlupdate.Options{
    CurrentVersion: "1.4.2",
    BaseDir:        appDataDir, // resolves relative install/key paths
    Config: &wmlupdate.Config{
        AppID:   "com.example.myapp",
        Channel: "stable",
        Source: wmlupdate.SourceConfig{
            Type:  wmlupdate.SourceGitHub,
            Owner: "acme",
            Repo:  "myapp",
        },
        AssetRules: []wmlupdate.AssetRule{
            {OS: "darwin", Arch: "arm64", Match: "myapp-{version}-macos-arm64.zip", Format: "zip"},
            {OS: "windows", Arch: "amd64", Match: "myapp-{version}-windows-amd64.zip", Format: "zip"},
            {OS: "linux", Arch: "amd64", Match: "myapp-{version}-linux-amd64.tar.gz", Format: "tar.gz"},
        },
        Install: wmlupdate.InstallConfig{
            Type:    wmlupdate.InstallDirectory,
            Paths:   map[string]string{
                "darwin":  "/Applications/MyApp.app",
                "windows": `C:\Program Files\MyApp`,
                "linux":   "/opt/myapp",
            },
            Preserve: []string{"data/**", "config/**"},
        },
    },
})

Programmatic durations use time.Duration; use ConfigPath for the JSON string form. BaseDir defaults to the process working directory for relative paths.

docs.title: Chains, mirrors, proxy and macOS
docs.text: SourceConfig.Sources supports ordered chains. SourceConfig.ManifestURLs, SourceConfig.AssetMirrors and DownloadConfig.Proxy expose the same failover and network options as the JSON configuration. InstallConfig.MacOS controls optional quarantine removal, ad-hoc signing and signer-change policy. See the configuration reference for semantics and security trade-offs.

docs.title: Current version
docs.text:
Pass the version compiled into the running application:

CurrentVersion: buildinfo.Version

It is the only reliable source. If omitted, the SDK falls back to recorded updater state and then Config.CurrentVersion. After an in-place successful Apply, the Updater updates its internal current version so the next Check is correct.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Options.Events receives:

Type Meaning EventLog Phase transition or diagnostic EventWarning Non-fatal security or recovery warning EventProgress Download bytes/total/percent

The callback runs synchronously on the updater's goroutine. Marshal UI updates to your own event loop if necessary. No callback is required.

docs.title: Applying
docs.text:
result, err := u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{})

Result statuses:

Status Meaning StatusUpdated Installed in-process StatusDownloaded install.type=external; artifact path returned StatusApplyScheduled Deferred helper scheduled

docs.title: Windows / running executable
docs.text:
Use deferred apply when the target is running or when the updater is replacing itself:

result, err := u.Apply(ctx, update, wmlupdate.ApplyOptions{
    Defer:    true,
    WaitPIDs: []int{os.Getpid()},
})

The call stages the update and starts a detached helper, then returns StatusApplyScheduled. The host should exit promptly. The helper waits for the listed PIDs, applies the journaled transaction and optionally relaunches via Config.Install.RelaunchPath.

docs.title: External installation
docs.text: With InstallExternal, Apply downloads and verifies the artifact and returns ArtifactPath; your application installs it. This keeps custom native installers, package managers or platform-specific logic outside the library.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Use Code for stable branching:

if err != nil {
    switch wmlupdate.Code(err) {
    case "no_update":
    case "integrity":
    case "source", "network":
    case "install":
    }
}

errors.Is(err, wmlupdate.ErrNoUpdate) also works. Codes match the CLI/API protocol: config, source, network, no_release, no_asset, integrity, install, rollback, locked, state, io, cancelled, no_update.

docs.title: Lifetime and concurrency
docs.text:
• New opens the state directory and configures an HTTP client.
  • Close releases idle HTTP connections. It does not cancel in-flight calls.
  • Check is read-only and safe to call concurrently.
  • Apply takes a per-application file lock; mutating calls are serialized.
  • An Update is an opaque checked snapshot. Call Check and Apply in the same process; do not serialize it or construct it manually.
  • Apply does not exit or restart the host. That remains your decision.
  • No daemon, service, web server or global registration is required.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
The library retains a backup according to Install.KeepBackups. The optional CLI exposes:

wml-update --config updater.json rollback

The SDK intentionally does not expose rollback in its minimal surface; use the CLI for operational recovery or keep an install.type=external path under your own control.

docs.title: Other languages
docs.text: A Go library cannot be loaded directly by Python, Node.js or Java. Those applications use the same engine through the sidecar CLI's NDJSON protocol or the loopback HTTP API. See integration. This is an adapter, not a requirement for Go applications.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: WML Update authenticates update metadata, verifies artifact bytes, checks network boundaries, extracts archives safely and replaces installations transactionally. It does not sandbox the application being updated, sign the new application, or protect a host that is already compromised.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text: Input Trust updater.json and CLI flags Trusted local configuration Environment values referenced by config Trusted local secrets Update source (HTTPS / GitHub API) Untrusted until authenticated Manifest contents Untrusted before signature verification Archive entries Untrusted Download bytes Untrusted until SHA-256 verification Local API caller Untrusted until bearer token check

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Self-hosted. With security.public_key_file (or inline public_key), the client downloads <manifest_url>.sig and verifies an Ed25519 signature over the exact raw manifest bytes before parsing. Missing or invalid signature is fatal. Without a configured key, metadata relies on TLS and is explicitly reported in documentation as less strong.

GitHub. Release metadata comes from the GitHub API over TLS with an optional access token. For artifact hashes the client uses, in order:

  1. A signed checksums.txt when a public key is configured (required).
  2. A checksums.txt asset when present.
  3. The GitHub API asset digest field.
  4. Nothing → the update is refused unless allow_unverified_assets is set.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
Every download requires a 64-hex SHA-256. The final file is not exposed until:

  • the expected byte size (when supplied) matches,
  • the SHA-256 matches,
  • the file is fsynced and atomically renamed from .part.

Hash mismatch deletes the partial file and retries within the configured budget. A checksum failure is reported as an integrity error.

docs.title: Signing keys
docs.text:
keygen writes a PKCS#8 Ed25519 private key with mode 0600 and a PKIX public key. The public key can be distributed inline as base64 raw bytes. The private key is a release credential:

  • keep it in a secret manager or protected CI secret,
  • never commit it,
  • never serve it from the update host,
  • rotate by shipping a client that trusts the new key before switching the channel key,
  • use a dedicated key per update channel if channels have different trust.

The signing format is detached Ed25519 over raw file bytes, signature encoded as standard base64 (raw 64-byte signatures are also accepted). This is easy to reproduce with OpenSSL or a small script and avoids canonical-JSON pitfalls.

docs.title: Network protections
docs.text:
• HTTPS only, except loopback or explicit security.allow_insecure_http.
  • Redirects are checked against scheme, allowlist and a 10-hop limit.
  • security.allowed_hosts applies to metadata, signatures, assets and every redirect target.
  • Authorization headers are not forwarded by Go's HTTP client across host changes. Self-hosted config headers are attached to assets only when the asset host exactly matches the manifest host.
  • Source-chain fallback URLs and asset mirrors never receive the winning source's credentials. A fallback download must match the checked SHA-256.
  • Response metadata bodies are size-limited (4 MiB manifests, 32 MiB GitHub response, 16 MiB checksums).
  • Downloads are bounded by download.max_bytes and verified sizes.
  • Retries are bounded and honor Retry-After.
  • Proxy settings follow Go's standard HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY environment unless download.proxy explicitly overrides them. A trusted proxy can observe destination hosts and URLs; it cannot substitute bytes because SHA-256 is still enforced.

docs.title: Archive extraction
docs.text:
• absolute POSIX paths and Windows volume/UNC paths rejected,
  • .. traversal rejected after normalization and after strip_components,
  • entries with NUL bytes rejected,
  • symlink targets must remain inside the extraction root,
  • writing through a symlinked parent is rejected (prevents symlink-first attacks),
  • hardlinks, devices, FIFOs and other special files rejected,
  • entry-count and expanded-size limits,
  • setuid/setgid bits are not applied,
  • files are created before restrictive directory modes are applied.

Symlinks are supported because macOS .app bundles require them. They are validated, not blindly trusted.

docs.title: Install target
docs.text:
Directory and file installs reject:

  • filesystem roots,
  • the user's home directory itself,
  • targets that are symlinks,
  • targets inside the state directory,
  • state directories inside the target,
  • staging/backup paths outside the target's parent.

This is defense in depth against a typo or malicious config. Configuration is trusted, but an updater with root privileges is a dangerous tool.

docs.title: Transactional behavior
docs.text:
The old installation is renamed to a backup before the staged tree is activated. The journal is written before each rename. Recovery restores the previous tree when a transaction was interrupted before the new tree was active.

command installers are intentionally outside this guarantee. They run with the updater's privileges and their rollback behavior belongs to the installer.

docs.title: macOS quarantine and ad-hoc signing
docs.text:
install.macos.remove_quarantine runs xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the installed target. This bypasses Gatekeeper's first-launch evaluation and weakens a user security boundary; enable it only when the update channel, signature and hashes are under your control.

install.macos.ad_hoc_sign runs codesign --force --deep --sign - on a .app. Ad-hoc signing can make an unsigned bundle launch, but it invalidates Developer ID signatures and notarization. Never enable it for a notarized distribution. Both options default off and only run when the updater runs on macOS.

For a signed installed .app, the updater verifies the staged bundle with codesign --verify --deep --strict and requires the same TeamIdentifier. allow_signer_change exists for an intentional certificate/team migration; do not use it to bypass an unexpected signer change.

docs.title: Windows helper
docs.text: --defer copies the updater executable to the state directory, not the target. The helper waits for selected PIDs, acquires the per-app lock, applies from the journal and writes a result file. This avoids executing a binary from inside the tree being replaced.

docs.title: Local HTTP API
docs.text:
• Bearer token required on every endpoint except /v1/health.
  • Constant-time token comparison.
  • Loopback bind by default; non-loopback binds require an explicit flag.
  • Body size limited to 1 MiB, server read/header timeouts set.
  • Unknown JSON fields rejected.
  • No CORS headers are added.
  • No token is logged. A generated token is printed once on the ready line and is not stored by the server.
  • Jobs keep only the last 512 events.
  • Remote deployment should use a TLS reverse proxy and an additional authentication layer.

The API can install software and write files as the updater user. Treat the token as equivalent to that user's update authority.

docs.title: Privileges
docs.text: Do not run the updater as root/system unless the install target requires it. If elevated installation is necessary, keep the updater and its state owned by the privileged account, protect the config and signing public key from unprivileged modification, and ensure the install target is not user-writable. A user who can modify updater.json, the public key, or the install target can redirect or replace updates.

docs.title: Residual risks
docs.text:
• A compromised signing key allows malicious releases until the key is rotated.
  • TLS-only self-hosted channels without a public key are vulnerable to a compromised host or CA.
  • allow_unverified_assets removes artifact authentication.
  • allow_insecure_http exposes metadata and artifacts to network attackers.
  • A malicious local user with write access to the install target or state directory can subvert the updater.
  • Replacing an application directory intentionally deletes files not preserved.
  • macOS code signing and Windows Authenticode are not performed; archives must be signed before packaging.
  • Command installers can do anything the updater user can do.
  • The local API has no per-endpoint authorization or rate limiting beyond the loopback default.
  • Source mirrors can deny service or serve different bytes; they cannot bypass the selected version or SHA-256 requirement. A mirror that serves a valid but malicious manifest still requires the configured Ed25519 key.
  • A configured proxy is a trusted network intermediary for availability and metadata; it does not replace artifact hashes.
  • Removing quarantine reduces Gatekeeper enforcement; ad-hoc signing destroys notarization.

docs.title: Verification checklist for integrators
docs.text:
• Pin/embed the Ed25519 public key and configure security.public_key_file.
  • Leave allow_unverified_assets and allow_insecure_http off.
  • Set allowed_hosts to the exact update infrastructure.
  • Install into an application-managed directory with least privilege.
  • Preserve only data your application owns.
  • Ship a rollback-tested installer.
  • Test the deferred flow on Windows.
  • Verify macOS bundles remain signed after packaging.
  • Protect API tokens and signing keys.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text: Please report vulnerabilities privately via GitHub Security Advisories for yxxbc/wmlUpdate. Do not open a public issue for a working exploit.

docs.title: Self-hosting updates
