docs.text: A self-hosted channel is just static files. No update server process is needed. This makes it easy to put behind nginx, Caddy, S3/R2, GitHub Pages, a CDN, or an internal object store.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
/var/www/updates/myapp/stable/
├── manifest.json
├── manifest.json.sig
├── checksums.txt
├── checksums.txt.sig
├── myapp-1.5.0-darwin-arm64.zip
├── myapp-1.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
└── myapp-1.5.0-windows-amd64.zip

Clients fetch only manifest.json and one matching asset. checksums.txt is useful for GitHub releases and manual verification; static clients trust the hashes inside the signed manifest.

docs.title: 1. Generate signing keys once
docs.text:
wml-update keygen --out-dir release-keys

Keep signing-key.pem in a secret manager / protected CI secret. Commit or distribute signing-key.pub.pem, or embed its base64 raw form in client config. The private key is 32 bytes of authority over every client channel: do not put it in the web root or a repository.

Key rotation: distribute a new client release that trusts the new public key before switching the channel to the new key. A client supports one public key.

docs.title: 2. Build platform artifacts
docs.text:
Use your normal build pipeline. Requirements:

  • Each asset is a zip, tar.gz, tar, or raw file supported by your install strategy.
  • Asset names are stable and understood by asset_rules, or the manifest carries os and arch.
  • Archives contain the exact directory tree the install strategy expects.
  • macOS .app bundles are signed and notarized before archiving. Replacing files inside an existing bundle invalidates its code signature.
  • Windows executables are Authenticode-signed before archiving if you rely on SmartScreen/enterprise trust.
  • install.strip_components matches whether the archive has a top-level folder.

publish can create archives from directories:

{
  "app_id": "com.example.myapp",
  "version": "1.5.0",
  "channel": "stable",
  "notes_file": "release-notes.md",
  "assets": [
    {"dir": "build/myapp-linux", "url": "myapp-1.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz", "os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "format": "tar.gz"},
    {"dir": "build/myapp-macos", "url": "myapp-1.5.0-darwin-arm64.zip", "os": "darwin", "arch": "arm64", "format": "zip"},
    {"dir": "build/myapp-windows", "url": "myapp-1.5.0-windows-amd64.zip", "os": "windows", "arch": "amd64", "format": "zip"}
  ]
}

dir archives the directory's contents. If your install expects a wrapper folder, pass a parent directory or set install.strip_components accordingly. Raw installers use path plus format.

docs.title: 3. Publish and sign
docs.text:
wml-update publish \
  --spec publish.json \
  --out dist/stable \
  --key release-keys/signing-key.pem \
  --base-url https://updates.example.com/myapp/stable

Outputs are deterministic enough to verify:

wml-update verify --manifest \
  --public-key-file release-keys/signing-key.pub.pem \
  dist/stable/manifest.json

--base-url is optional. Without it, asset URLs are relative to the manifest, which is preferable when the host or CDN domain may change.

docs.title: 4. Upload atomically
docs.text:
Order matters:

  1. Upload new versioned assets.
  2. Upload manifest.json and manifest.json.sig last.
  3. Keep the previous version's files available.

A client may fetch the manifest at any instant. Publishing the manifest before its assets creates a window where every update fails. Some object stores allow copy-and-swap or versioned objects; if not, uploading assets first is sufficient.

Deploy manifests with a short cache lifetime, for example Cache-Control: no-cache or max-age=60, must-revalidate. Versioned assets can be immutable:

Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

The updater honors ETag/Last-Modified and uses conditional requests.

docs.title: nginx
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name updates.example.com;

    root /var/www/updates;

    location = /myapp/stable/manifest.json {
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate";
        types { }
        default_type application/json;
    }

    location = /myapp/stable/manifest.json.sig {
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate";
        default_type text/plain;
    }

    location ~* \.(zip|tar\.gz|exe|msi|pkg|dmg)$ {
        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
    }

    # Optional basic auth for a private channel. The client supports
    # source.headers; see "Private channels" below.
    # auth_basic "updates";
    # auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/updates.htpasswd;
}

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
updates.example.com {
    root * /var/www/updates
    file_server
    header /myapp/stable/manifest.json Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate"
    header /myapp/stable/manifest.json.sig Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate"
}

docs.title: 6. Client configuration
docs.text:
{
  "app_id": "com.example.myapp",
  "channel": "stable",
  "source": {
    "type": "static",
    "manifest_url": "https://updates.example.com/myapp/stable/manifest.json"
  },
  "asset_rules": [
    {"os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "match": "myapp-*-linux-amd64.tar.gz", "format": "tar.gz"},
    {"os": "darwin", "arch": "arm64", "match": "myapp-*-darwin-arm64.zip", "format": "zip"},
    {"os": "windows", "arch": "amd64", "match": "myapp-*-windows-amd64.zip", "format": "zip"}
  ],
  "install": {
    "type": "directory",
    "paths": {
      "linux": "/opt/myapp",
      "darwin": "/Applications/MyApp.app",
      "windows": "C:\\Program Files\\MyApp"
    },
    "keep_backups": 1
  },
  "security": {
    "public_key_file": "keys/signing-key.pub.pem",
    "allowed_hosts": ["updates.example.com", "cdn.example.com"]
  }
}

If assets are moved to a CDN host, include that host in allowed_hosts and make sure the signed manifest's asset URLs resolve there.

docs.title: Private channels
docs.text:
Static hosts can require a bearer token or basic auth:

"source": {
  "type": "static",
  "manifest_url": "https://updates.example.com/private/stable/manifest.json",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer ${UPDATE_TOKEN}"
  }
}

${UPDATE_TOKEN} must exist at runtime. The updater errors rather than sending a silently empty token. Headers are sent to the manifest and same-host assets only. If your assets are on a different host, use signed URLs generated by the manifest tooling or a CDN that does not require the secret.

Do not embed long-lived credentials in a distributed client if the channel is public. Prefer a short-lived token issued by your backend, supplied through the environment.

docs.title: Mirrors and failover
docs.text:
A single static host is a single point of failure. Deploy the same manifest and assets to multiple hosts and configure either:

  • source.manifest_urls with ordered URLs for the same static channel;
  • a source.type: chain containing GitHub, static mirrors, jsDelivr, ghproxy, Gitee and your own site;
  • asset_mirrors URL templates for artifact hosts.

Fallback downloads must match the originally checked SHA-256. Mirrors cannot change the version or bytes. See configuration.

docs.title: Multiple channels
docs.text:
Use separate directories, manifests and client channel values:

stable/manifest.json
beta/manifest.json
nightly/manifest.json

The client enforces that the manifest's channel matches the configured channel. GitHub channels are derived from prerelease flags instead.

docs.title: Rollback at the service level
docs.text:
Clients roll back with wml-update rollback using the local backup. To roll back a release for all clients, publish the previous version as a new higher version rather than republishing an old version number. SemVer comparison means clients already on the broken version will not downgrade to an older version number.

For an emergency, ship 1.5.1 containing the previous code.

docs.title: Signing in CI
docs.text:
- name: Sign and publish
  env:
    WML_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.WML_SIGNING_KEY }}
  run: |
    umask 077
    printf '%s' "$WML_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing-key.pem"
    wml-update publish \
      --spec publish.json \
      --out dist/stable \
      --key "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing-key.pem"
    rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing-key.pem"

Upload the output with your cloud provider's CLI. Keep the public key in the repository or client config, never the private key.

docs.title: Verification checklist
docs.text:
• manifest.json.sig validates with the shipped public key.
  • Every asset's sha256 and size match what was built.
  • Asset URLs are reachable by clients and are in allowed_hosts.
  • channel matches.
  • The install target is writable by the updating user.
  • The archive's top-level layout matches strip_components.
  • macOS bundle signatures remain valid after update.
  • A test update succeeds on all three platforms, including rollback.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: You do not need to create an external package to test WML Update. The repository contains unit, integration and end-to-end tests for the engine and the public SDK.

docs.title: Automated test suite
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate.git
cd wmlUpdate
make test

This runs:

  • strict SemVer, config, manifest and signing tests
  • archive traversal, symlink, hardlink and expansion defenses
  • source discovery for GitHub Releases, static mirrors, ordered chains and download failover
  • resumable downloads, checksums and HTTP policy
  • transactional directory/file installs, backups, recovery and rollback
  • the public SDK and local HTTP API
  • an external-consumer compile check is not part of the suite, but the SDK tests exercise the public API directly

Race detector:

make race

CI runs the suite on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, plus go vet, govulncheck, cross-compilation and the SDK playground. The same playground can be run on every platform with make e2e.

docs.title: One-command local end-to-end test
docs.text:
make e2e
# or
go run ./examples/playground

The playground:

  1. creates a temporary v1 application tree;
  2. builds a v2 zip;
  3. computes its SHA-256 and writes a loopback manifest;
  4. serves it through an in-process HTTP server;
  5. calls the public SDK with Check, then Apply;
  6. verifies the installed file and the post-update Check;
  7. prints local SDK end-to-end test passed.

Use -keep to inspect the generated source, target, state, backup and logs:

go run ./examples/playground -keep

The playground uses an unsigned loopback manifest to keep the harness small. Ed25519 manifest and checksum signatures are covered by the automated tests and are expected in production.

docs.title: Test your own configuration
docs.text:
For a real config, use the CLI diagnostics first:

wml-update --config updater.json doctor --current-version 1.4.2
wml-update --config updater.json --json check --current-version 1.4.2
wml-update --config updater.json update --dry-run --current-version 1.4.2
wml-update --config updater.json fetch --output /tmp/app.zip --current-version 1.4.2

fetch performs discovery, download and SHA-256 verification without touching the install tree. Inspect the artifact, then run update when ready.

To test a different platform without leaving your machine, use --os and --arch; install paths and asset rules are resolved for that target.

docs.title: Test a self-hosted release locally
docs.text:
wml-update keygen --out-dir keys
wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out public/stable --key keys/signing-key.pem
python3 -m http.server 18080 --directory public

Then point a temporary config at:

http://127.0.0.1:18080/stable/manifest.json

and run check or update. Loopback HTTP is allowed by the default security policy. Use a temporary state_dir and install target for the test.

docs.title: Test a GitHub release
docs.text:
Create a scratch repository or a prerelease in an existing one, attach the platform archives and checksums.txt, then:

wml-update --config test-updater.json check --current-version 0.0.1
wml-update --config test-updater.json fetch --output /tmp/artifact

For private repositories, set the token environment variable named by source.token_env. Do not put the token in the JSON file.

docs.title: Test Windows deferred apply
docs.text:
On Windows, with the target process running:

wml-update --config updater.json update --defer --wait-pid <pid> --json

The parent returns apply_scheduled; the application should exit. The helper writes its outcome to:

<state_dir>/plans/<plan_id>.json.result

The same behavior is available from the SDK with ApplyOptions{Defer: true, WaitPIDs: ...}.

docs.title: Test the release CLI
docs.text:
wml-update keygen --out-dir /tmp/test-keys
wml-update publish --spec publish.json --out /tmp/test-public --key /tmp/test-keys/signing-key.pem
wml-update verify --manifest \
  --public-key-file /tmp/test-keys/signing-key.pub.pem \
  /tmp/test-public/manifest.json

This exercises archive creation, hashing, manifest validation and detached signature verification without a network service.

docs.title: Test the SDK from another module
docs.text:
If you are testing your own integration, a small external module is the most realistic check:

mkdir sdk-consumer && cd sdk-consumer
go mod init example.com/sdk-consumer
go get github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate@v1.1.0

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    wmlupdate "github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate"
)

func main() {
    u, err := wmlupdate.New(wmlupdate.Options{
        ConfigPath:     "updater.json",
        CurrentVersion: "1.4.2",
    })
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer u.Close()

    update, err := u.Check(context.Background())
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    fmt.Println(update.Available, update.Version)
}

The included examples/go is this pattern in runnable form.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with:

wml-update --config updater.json doctor --current-version 1.2.3
wml-update --config updater.json status

doctor checks config parsing, state directory writability, install parent, target symlinks, signing key loading, pending transactions and source connectivity.

docs.title: No configuration file found
docs.text: The updater looks for updater.json, .wml-update.json and wml-update.json in the current directory, or WML_UPDATE_CONFIG. Relative paths inside the config resolve against the config file, not the shell's current directory. Prefer an absolute --config path from a desktop app.

docs.title: current version is unknown
docs.text:
Pass the application's compiled version:

wml-update update --current-version 1.2.3

current_version in JSON and the recorded state are fallbacks. A stale state file can cause repeated or missed updates; the flag is authoritative.

docs.title: GitHub API rate limit
docs.text:
Set source.token_env and provide a token at runtime:

export GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_...
wml-update check

The error mentions the rate limit. If token_env is set but missing, the updater fails rather than proceeding anonymously. Token scopes: public repositories need public read; private repositories need release read access.

docs.title: no_asset: no matching release asset
docs.text:
The error lists available asset names. Add an explicit asset_rules entry:

{"os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "match": "myapp-{version}-linux-x86_64.tar.gz", "format": "tar.gz"}

Check:

  • {version} has no leading v; use {tag} if your filename includes it.
  • Asset names are case-sensitive for path.Match.
  • The release is not a draft.
  • The release is not flagged prerelease when channel is stable.
  • --os / --arch are not overriding the platform unexpectedly.

docs.title: no_release: nothing eligible
docs.text:
• Tag is valid strict SemVer after tag_prefix is removed.
  • Stable channel excludes prereleases.
  • Draft releases are always skipped.
  • The repository has releases, not only tags.

Use --channel beta or source.include_prerelease: true for prereleases.

docs.title: Signature failures
docs.text:
manifest signature: signature verification failed
  • The public key must match the private key that signed manifest.json.
  • The signature must cover the exact bytes served. Re-run wml-update publish; editing manifest.json after signing invalidates it.
  • For GitHub, both checksums.txt and checksums.txt.sig must be release assets with the configured names.
  • A .sig file may be base64 text or raw 64 bytes; both are accepted.
  • Verify manually:
wml-update verify --manifest --public-key-file key.pub manifest.json

docs.title: Checksum mismatch
docs.text:
The manifest or checksum file expects different bytes than the server returned. Common causes:

  • Asset overwritten after publishing
  • CDN serving stale/manipulated content
  • Signed manifest points at an old filename with new bytes
  • Partial upload

Republish artifacts, then manifest. Clear .part files if you suspect a stale resume:

find "$STATE_DIR/downloads" -name '*.part' -delete

A truncated download reports unexpected EOF as an integrity error and retries from scratch.

docs.title: HTTP refused / insecure URL
docs.text:
Plain HTTP to a non-loopback host is refused. Use HTTPS. For isolated test networks only:

"security": { "allow_insecure_http": true }

docs.title: Host allowlist rejected
docs.text:
Add every host used, including redirect targets:

"allowed_hosts": [
  "api.github.com",
  "github.com",
  "objects.githubusercontent.com",
  "release-assets.githubusercontent.com",
  "updates.example.com"
]

For GitHub, the exact asset redirect host may differ. Check the error message, which names the rejected host.

docs.title: Directory install fails: file in use / access denied (Windows)
docs.text:
Close the application and update, or use the deferred flow:

wml-update update --defer --wait-pid <PID> --json

The application should exit after it receives apply_scheduled. A detached helper performs the replacement and can relaunch via install.relaunch_path.

If it still fails, another process (antivirus, DLL host, crash reporter) holds a file. Check the target directory with Process Explorer or close the locking process.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text:
The updater user must be able to:

  • create staging and backup directories next to the install target,
  • rename the target,
  • write inside the target.

/Applications, /opt and C:\Program Files commonly require elevation. Prefer per-user install locations. If elevation is unavoidable, run the updater elevated and protect its config/public key from unprivileged modification.

docs.title: another update is already running
docs.text:
A lock exists at <state_dir>/update.lock. Find the other updater process or wait. Locks are advisory and released when the process exits; a stale file is harmless.

If the lock holder crashed during an install, the next mutating command recovers the journal automatically. Check wml-update status for Pending install.

docs.title: Pending transaction after a crash
docs.text:
The next update or rollback runs recovery while holding the lock:

  • An interrupted swap restores the previous version.
  • A swap that completed before the journal update is finalized.
  • A command installer journal cannot be verified and is cleared with a warning.

If recovery itself fails, inspect state.json and the sibling .wml-update-backup-* directory. Do not delete a backup until you know which version is live. A manual restore is:

rename target -> target.failed
rename .wml-update-backup-<app>-<id> -> target

Run wml-update status before and after.

docs.title: No backup available for rollback
docs.text:
• The install was a command or external install (no backup is created).
  • The previous update already rolled back.
  • The backup directory was removed manually.

docs.title: mac app fails Gatekeeper after update
docs.text:
Replacing files changes a macOS bundle. The new bundle must be signed and notarized before packaging. WML Update does not re-sign or strip quarantine. Build, sign, notarize, staple, then archive. Verify with:

codesign --verify --deep --strict /Applications/MyApp.app
spctl --assess --type execute /Applications/MyApp.app

docs.title: Command installer failed
docs.text:
Run with --json and inspect the log event containing captured output. The command is not executed through a shell, so pipes/redirection do not work. Wrap complex logic in a script and point install.command at it.

Check placeholders:

  • {artifact} is the verified downloaded file.
  • {install_dir} may be empty for command installs without a configured path.
  • Use the platform-appropriate installer, for example msiexec.exe /i {artifact} /qn on Windows.

docs.title: Local API returns 401
docs.text:
• Use Authorization: Bearer <token> or X-WML-Token: <token>.
  • A generated token is printed only in the serve --json ready line.
  • If you use --token-env, the variable must be set in the server's environment.
  • Tokens under 16 characters are rejected.

docs.title: Local API returns 409 job_conflict
docs.text: Only one update, fetch or rollback job may run at a time. Poll the current job or cancel it before starting another.

docs.title: SSE stream is empty
docs.text: The stream closes when the job has finished and all events have been delivered. Connect while the job is running, or poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} for the complete snapshot. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID to resume.

docs.title: State file is corrupt
docs.text: The updater fails rather than silently resetting. Inspect the file. If no transaction is pending and the recorded version is no longer useful, stop the app, back up the file, then remove it; the next run recreates state. Never delete state while pending is set without first inspecting the target and backup.

docs.title: Debugging with --json
docs.text:
JSON mode is the best source of truth:

wml-update --config updater.json --json update --current-version 1.0.0 2>stderr.log

Every progress/log/warning is a JSON line on stdout; stderr.log contains any human diagnostics. The terminal error object has a stable code suitable for support tickets.

docs.title: Versioning and compatibility
docs.text: WML Update follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

docs.title: Current status
docs.text:
• v1.1.0 is the current stable release. v1.0.0 remains available as a historical release; both freeze the public Go API and package import path.
  • v0.1.0 was the initial public preview. It remains permanently available for reproducibility and must not be retagged or moved.
  • main may contain changes that are not in the latest release. The documentation site publishes dev separately from released versions.
  • The nightly workflow publishes prerelease builds such as v1.2.0-nightly.20261028.42.1. They are valid Go module tags but are never latest and are not selected by a stable client.

docs.title: One ordering version, several metadata axes
docs.text:
A single SemVer is still the right identity and ordering key for the Go module, the CLI and the update protocol. It is not the only metadata a frequent release process needs.

Use orthogonal axes:

Axis Example Purpose SemVer release 1.0.3, 1.1.0-beta.2 update identity and ordering channel stable, beta, nightly who receives the build build/commit 20261028.3, git SHA display, support and provenance published time RFC 3339 feed ordering and release notes

Rules for frequent builds:

  • Every build that clients can install gets a unique SemVer. Prefer a monotonic patch counter (v1.0.1341) for stable builds or a pre-release (v1.1.0-nightly.20261028.3) for nightly builds.
  • Never reuse a version for different bytes.
  • Never use +build metadata as the only difference: SemVer ordering ignores it, so the updater would treat the builds as equal.
  • Publish stable, beta and nightly through separate manifest URLs/channels. A nightly tag must not be promoted to stable clients by accident.
  • Keep one tag for the Go module and CLI release of the same commit. If the CLI and SDK ever need independent release cadences, split the CLI into its own Go module and tag path rather than inventing two versions for one module.
  • Versioned documentation follows tags with mike; dev is not a release.

This is why a single number is not insufficient by itself: it remains the ordering key. The missing pieces for frequent updates are unique version bumps, channels and provenance/build metadata, not a second competing version number.

See frequent releases for the feed/staging model.

docs.title: Compatibility promise from v1.0.0
docs.text:
The stable public surface is:

  • package github.com/yxxbc/wmlUpdate
  • New, (*Updater).Check, (*Updater).Apply, (*Updater).Close
  • Options, Config, Update, ApplyOptions, Result, Event
  • documented JSON configuration and NDJSON/HTTP protocols

Within a major version:

  • minor releases add fields, sources, options and commands;
  • patch releases fix defects without changing documented behavior;
  • major releases may change or remove exported identifiers, method signatures or documented protocol semantics;
  • new configuration fields are additive; unknown fields continue to be rejected so typos fail loudly.

Go guarantees:

  • minimum Go version is declared in go.mod and may only increase in a minor release;
  • the module path, import path and package name are stable for the v1 line;
  • pre-built CLI archives are provided for Windows, macOS and Linux (amd64, arm64).

docs.title: Tags are immutable
docs.text:
Published tags are treated as immutable. Do not move, delete or reuse a version tag: Go module proxies, checksums and downstream lock files may already have cached it. If a release must be withdrawn, publish a new version and use the Go retract directive if appropriate; never rewrite history behind an existing tag.

Pre-releases use SemVer identifiers, for example v1.1.0-rc.1 or v1.2.0-nightly.20261028.42.1. They are not selected by default and should be treated as unstable. Nightly tags are immutable too; do not reuse a nightly version or delete it to "clean up" after clients may have cached it.

docs.title: Documentation versions
docs.text:
The documentation site publishes:

  • released versions, e.g. 1.0.0;
  • latest, an alias for the newest stable release;
  • dev, built from main.

The version selector is provided by mike. Users on a tagged release should read the matching documentation version, not dev.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
1. make check, make race, and the SDK playground pass on the host.
  2. CI passes on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows.
  3. A real consumer builds against the release candidate.
  4. Update CHANGELOG.md and version references.
  5. Create an annotated tag, push it, and let the release workflow build, sign checksums.txt and publish assets.
  6. Verify the detached signature with signing/release-signing-key.pub.pem.
  7. Deploy the matching documentation version with mike.

docs.title: Architecture decisions
docs.text:
• 0001: Go static binary
  • 0002: subprocess NDJSON and local HTTP — superseded as the primary surface by 0005
  • 0003: transactional install
  • 0004: supply-chain verification
  • 0005: SDK-first public API
  • 0006: ordered source chains

docs.title: ADR 0001: Implement the updater in Go as one static binary
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The updater must run on Windows, macOS and Linux, frequently as a subprocess of applications written in unrelated languages. It needs HTTP, archive handling, cryptography, filesystem transactions, process control and a CLI.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Go with CGO_ENABLED=0 and build one binary per OS/architecture. Keep the runtime dependency set small: Cobra for the CLI, gofrs/flock for cross-platform file locks, doublestar for preserve globs, and x/sys for Windows process checks.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Distribution is a single archive; no language runtime, package manager or shared library is required on the client.
  • Cross-compilation is part of CI and release automation.
  • The updater is easy to call from any language as a subprocess.
  • Dependency review is small and bounded.
  • A Go toolchain is required to build, but not to use.

docs.title: ADR 0002: Expose subprocess NDJSON first, loopback HTTP second
docs.text:
• Status: superseded by ADR 0005 for the primary integration surface; the NDJSON/HTTP adapters remain supported
  • Date: 2026-10-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: "Any language" must not mean maintaining an SDK per language. Desktop UIs also need progress, cancellation and long-lived state.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Make the CLI with --json the primary protocol: one JSON object per line, terminal result or error, stable error codes and exit codes. Offer an optional loopback HTTP server for applications that want asynchronous jobs, polling, cancellation and SSE. Both surfaces share the same engine and result model.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A language only needs process execution and a JSON parser.
  • Progress can be streamed without a network server.
  • The HTTP API adds a security surface, so it requires a bearer token, binds loopback by default and limits request sizes.
  • API jobs are intentionally in-memory; durable state remains state.json.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Replace directories transactionally with sibling backups
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Replacing application files in place can leave a half-updated application after a crash. On Windows, running binaries cannot be renamed or deleted. Users need a rollback path.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Stage the complete new tree in a sibling directory. Journal the transaction in state. Rename the old target to a sibling backup, rename the stage into place, then record success. On failure or next start, restore the backup. Retain the most recent backups.

For Windows, allow a detached helper copied to the state directory to wait for the application PID and perform the same journaled apply.

Treat a directory install as a unit, not as a merge. Add explicit preserve globs for data that must survive. Use a separate single-file strategy where appropriate.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Swaps are atomic on a filesystem and recoverable after crashes.
  • The target must be a dedicated application-managed directory; user content is removed unless preserved.
  • Backups consume disk equal to the previous installation; retention is bounded.
  • A running Windows app must opt into --defer; direct replacement fails with a clear message.
  • Command installers cannot be rolled back by the updater.

docs.title: ADR 0004: Require hashes, support Ed25519 detached signatures
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: HTTPS protects transit, not a compromised release account or host. JSON signing schemes often require canonicalization, which is easy to implement incorrectly across languages. Users need a simple, reproducible trust anchor.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Require SHA-256 for every artifact. Refuse downloads without one unless the operator explicitly sets allow_unverified_assets.
  • Use detached Ed25519 signatures over exact file bytes, encoded as standard base64. Sign self-hosted manifests and GitHub checksum files.
  • When a public key is configured, signatures are mandatory and a missing signature is fatal.
  • Prefer signed checksum files over per-artifact signatures: one signature authenticates all hashes and works for any number of assets.
  • Enforce HTTPS and optional host allowlists on every request and redirect.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• There is no canonical-JSON ambiguity: bytes in, bytes verified.
  • Signing is trivial from Go, OpenSSL, Python or CI.
  • Key management becomes a release responsibility; docs cover storage and rotation.
  • Existing GitHub releases without a digest or checksums fail unless the operator opts into unverified downloads or rebuilds their release process.

docs.title: ADR 0005: Make the Go SDK the primary integration surface
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The first implementation exposed the updater primarily as a standalone binary with an NDJSON/HTTP protocol. That works for every language, but Go applications had to ship and spawn a process and model updater lifecycle themselves. The product goal is a lightweight dependency with minimal intrusion: expose check and apply, not a framework.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Publish a Go package at the module root with a deliberately small API: New, Check, Apply, Close.
  • Check returns an opaque checked snapshot. Apply installs that exact snapshot, without re-fetching mutable source metadata; artifact bytes are still downloaded and verified.
  • Keep the host in control of lifecycle, UI, prompts and restart. The library never exits or restarts the host process.
  • Keep the standalone CLI and HTTP API as optional adapters for non-Go languages, process isolation and operational tooling.
  • Keep release packaging/signing in the CLI (publish, keygen, sign, verify) so release automation does not need a language binding.
  • Avoid daemon requirements, global registration, framework hooks and required application directory conventions.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Go applications integrate with a few lines and no process boundary.
  • Other languages retain a supported path through the sidecar protocol.
  • There are two public contracts to keep compatible: the Go API and the NDJSON/ HTTP event protocol. Both are tested from the same engine.
  • Update values are intentionally opaque and not serializable; check and apply must happen in one process.
  • A future native binding for another language can layer on the engine or the sidecar without changing the Go API.

docs.title: ADR 0006: Ordered source chains with hash-bound download failover
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A single source URL makes updates unavailable when a host, API, or asset CDN is blocked or down. Applications in restricted networks commonly need mirrors (jsDelivr, ghproxy, Gitee, a website) and automatic fallback. Naively switching to another source can install a different version or unauthenticated bytes.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Add source.type: chain with an ordered sources array. Metadata is fetched from each source until one returns a valid, authenticated release.
  • Add manifest_urls for static mirror metadata and asset_mirrors URL templates for artifact hosts.
  • On artifact download failure, try mirrors and later chain sources only when they offer the exact selected version and a SHA-256 equal to the checked artifact.
  • Never forward source credentials or GitHub tokens to a different mirror host.
  • Keep signatures and hashes mandatory; mirrors affect availability only.
  • Document first-success semantics: a reachable but stale first mirror wins over a newer fallback. Operators should keep mirrors synchronized.

docs.title: Consequences

• A blocked GitHub API or asset host no longer makes updates impossible.
  • Fallback downloads require an extra metadata fetch only after a failure.
  • Mirrors cannot cause downgrade or byte substitution without breaking the hash.
  • Configuration is more verbose, but chain and mirror templates are optional and backward compatible.
  • Nested chains are rejected to keep semantics and loop risk bounded.
